records.source: וּבְנֵ֨י רְאוּבֵ֥ן בְּכֽוֹר־יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ כִּ֣י ה֣וּא הַבְּכוֹר֒ וּֽבְחַלְּלוֹ֙ יְצוּעֵ֣י אָבִ֔יו נִתְּנָה֙ בְּכֹ֣רָת֔וֹ לִבְנֵ֥י יוֹסֵ֖ף בֶּן־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֥א לְהִתְיַחֵ֖שׂ לַבְּכֹרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Reuben, firstborn of Israel, for he [was] the firstborn, but when he profaned [the] beds of his father was given his birthright to [the] sons of Joseph son of Israel, and not to be enrolled by genealogy according to the birthright;
pieces: The sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel—he was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed, his birthright went to the sons of Joseph son of Israel, and the genealogy is not set out according to the birthright;

L.1: And [the] sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel—for he [was] the firstborn, but when he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel, and [one is] not to be enrolled in the genealogy according to the birthright;

R.1: This is the family of Reuben, Israel's oldest son. Reuben was born first, but he slept with one of his father's wives and so brought shame on his father's bed. Because of this, his rights as the oldest son were given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel. So the family records are not set out by who had the rights of the oldest son.

decisions.choice: he defiled his father's bed: Reuben lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine
decisions.reason: This looks back to Genesis 35:22, where Reuben lay with Bilhah, and to Jacob's words in Genesis 49:4, which use the same verb "defile" and the same word for his father's bed. Jacob there took from Reuben the first place that was his by birth (49:3-4).

decisions.choice: the birthright given to the sons of Joseph: the firstborn's double share
decisions.reason: The firstborn received a double share of his father's inheritance (Deuteronomy 21:17). Jacob adopted Joseph's two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, as his own (Genesis 48:5), so Joseph's line received two tribal shares where every other son received one.

decisions.choice: not to be enrolled according to the birthright: the genealogy is not arranged by the birthright
alternatives: Reuben is not listed as firstborn
Joseph is not listed as firstborn
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has an infinitive with no stated subject: "and not to be enrolled according to the birthright". Read as impersonal, it explains why the genealogies do not put the holder of the birthright first: Judah, not Joseph, leads the lists (chapters 2-4), as verse 2 explains. It may instead mean that Reuben is not listed as firstborn, or that Joseph, though he had the birthright, is not listed as firstborn.

decisions.choice: the list breaks off for an explanation and resumes in verse 3
decisions.reason: After "the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel" the writer stops to explain why Reuben, though firstborn, does not come first in these genealogies. The explanation runs to the end of verse 2, and verse 3 starts the list again with the same words.

decisions.choice: dashes around the explanation
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced mark the break in the sentence with a dash here and at the end of verse 2 (m4). Readable makes the explanation into sentences of its own.

decisions.choice: slept with one of his father's wives and so brought shame on his father's bed
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the picture of defiling the bed refers to (m1). Bilhah was a secondary wife of Jacob (Genesis 30:4).

records.heading: The descendants of Reuben

records.source: כִּ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ גָּבַ֣ר בְּאֶחָ֔יו וּלְנָגִ֖יד מִמֶּ֑נּוּ וְהַבְּכֹרָ֖ה לְיוֹסֵֽף׃ס
records.gloss: For Judah was strong among his brothers, and [a] ruler [was] from him, and the birthright [was] to Joseph—
pieces: for Judah grew stronger than his brothers, and a ruler came from him, though the birthright belonged to Joseph—

L.2: for Judah grew strong among his brothers, and a ruler [came] from him, but the birthright [was] Joseph's—

R.2: Judah became the strongest of the brothers, and a leader came from his family. But the rights of the oldest son belonged to Joseph.

decisions.choice: ruler (nagid): the leader chosen to rule God's people, here David and the kings after him
decisions.reason: Nagid is the word used when God appoints Saul and David to lead his people (1 Samuel 9:16; 13:14; 2 Samuel 7:8). David says that God chose Judah to be ruler and chose him from Judah (28:4).

decisions.choice: Judah grew strong among his brothers
decisions.reason: Jacob's blessing said Judah's brothers would bow to him and the scepter would not leave him (Genesis 49:8-10). Chronicles sees this fulfilled in the kings of David's line, which is why Judah heads the genealogies.

decisions.choice: but the birthright was Joseph's: rule and birthright went to different sons
decisions.reason: Reuben's firstborn rights were divided: the double share went to Joseph (verse 1), and the leadership to Judah.

decisions.choice: leader
decisions.reason: As across Samuel, Kings and Chronicles, nagid is "ruler" at Literal and Balanced and "leader" at Readable.

records.source: בְּנֵ֥י רְאוּבֵ֖ן בְּכ֣וֹר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל חֲנ֥וֹךְ וּפַלּ֖וּא חֶצְר֥וֹן וְכַרְמִֽי׃
records.gloss: [The] sons of Reuben, firstborn of Israel: Hanoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi.
pieces: the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron and Carmi.

L.3: the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi.

R.3: Reuben, Israel's oldest son, had these sons: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron and Carmi.

decisions.choice: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron and Carmi: the same four sons as the earlier lists
decisions.reason: The names match Genesis 46:9, Exodus 6:14 and Numbers 26:5-6. The words "the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel" pick up the list where verse 1 left it.

records.source: בְּנֵ֖י יוֹאֵ֑ל שְׁמַֽעְיָ֥ה בְנ֛וֹ גּ֥וֹג בְּנ֖וֹ שִׁמְעִ֥י בְנֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: [The] sons of Joel: Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son,
pieces: The descendants of Joel: Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son,

L.4: [The] sons of Joel: Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son,

R.4: Joel's son was Shemaiah, Shemaiah's son was Gog, and Gog's son was Shimei.

decisions.choice: the sons of Joel: a line of descent, each man the son of the one before
decisions.reason: The list runs from father to son, from Joel to Beerah (verse 6). The writer does not say how Joel was descended from Reuben.

decisions.choice: descendants (Balanced); each father named (Readable)
decisions.reason: Because the list is a chain of generations rather than brothers (m1), Balanced says "descendants" and Readable names each father.

records.source: מִיכָ֥ה בְנ֛וֹ רְאָיָ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ בַּ֥עַל בְּנֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son,
pieces: Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son,

L.5: Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son,

R.5: Shimei's son was Micah, Micah's son was Reaiah, and Reaiah's son was Baal.

decisions.choice: Baal: a personal name
decisions.reason: Baal means "master" or "lord". It appears as a man's name here and in 8:30, as it does inside other names (Merib-baal, 8:34), alongside its use for the Canaanite god.

records.source: בְּאֵרָ֣ה בְנ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶגְלָ֔ה תִּלְּגַ֥ת פִּלְנְאֶ֖סֶר מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשֻּׁ֑ר ה֥וּא נָשִׂ֖יא לָרֽאוּבֵנִֽי׃
records.gloss: Beerah his son, whom exiled Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria; he [was] leader of the Reubenite[s].
pieces: and Beerah his son, whom Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria took away into exile. He was a leader of the Reubenites.

L.6: Beerah his son, whom Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria exiled; he [was] a leader of the Reubenites.

R.6: Baal's son was Beerah. He was a leader of the tribe of Reuben, and Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria took him away as a captive.

decisions.choice: Tilgath-pilneser: the king called Tiglath-pileser in 2 Kings
decisions.reason: Chronicles spells the name of this king of Assyria Tilgath-pilneser (also verse 26; 2 Chronicles 28:20), where 2 Kings spells it Tiglath-pileser (2 Kings 15:29; 16:7). He is the same king, Tiglath-pileser the third, who took the lands east of the Jordan and the north of Israel and carried their people away (2 Kings 15:29).

decisions.choice: leader (nasi'): a chief of the tribe
decisions.reason: Nasi' is the word for the tribal leaders of Numbers (Numbers 1:16; 7:2). Beerah was a head of the Reubenites when the Assyrians came.

decisions.choice: Tilgath-pilneser (Literal); Tiglath-pileser (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the spelling Chronicles uses; Balanced and Readable use the form found in 2 Kings, so that readers recognize the king (m1).

records.source: וְאֶחָיו֙ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֔יו בְּהִתְיַחֵ֖שׂ לְתֹלְדוֹתָ֑ם הָרֹ֥אשׁ יְעִיאֵ֖ל וּזְכַרְיָֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And his brothers by his clans, in [the] enrolling of their generations: the head Jeiel, and Zechariah,
pieces: His relatives by their clans, as their generations were recorded in the genealogy, were Jeiel the chief, Zechariah,

L.7: And his brothers by his clans, when their generations were enrolled in the genealogy: the chief, Jeiel, and Zechariah,

R.7: His relatives, clan by clan, as they were listed in the family records, were Jeiel the leader, Zechariah,

decisions.choice: his brothers: his relatives in the tribe
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means kinsmen of Beerah's tribe, the heads of other Reubenite clans, not sons of his own father.

decisions.choice: enrolled in the genealogy: entered in the tribal register
decisions.reason: This verb, used mostly in Chronicles, Ezra and Nehemiah, means to be recorded by descent in the family register (verses 1 and 17; Ezra 2:62).

decisions.choice: relatives
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "relatives" for "brothers" (m1).

records.source: וּבֶ֨לַע֙ בֶּן־עָזָ֔ז בֶּן־שֶׁ֖מַע בֶּן־יוֹאֵ֑ל ה֚וּא יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בַּעֲרֹעֵ֔ר וְעַד־נְב֖וֹ וּבַ֥עַל מְעֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: and Bela son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel; he [was] dwelling in Aroer and as far as Nebo and Baal-meon.
pieces: and Bela son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel. He lived in Aroer and as far as Nebo and Baal-meon.

L.8: and Bela son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel; he [was] dwelling in Aroer and as far as Nebo and Baal-meon.

R.8: and Bela son of Azaz, the son of Shema, the son of Joel. Bela's family lived in Aroer and in the land as far as Nebo and Baal-meon.

decisions.choice: Aroer, Nebo and Baal-meon: towns of Reuben east of the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Aroer stood on the Arnon gorge at the southern edge of Reuben's land (Joshua 13:16). Nebo and Baal-meon were towns the Reubenites rebuilt (Numbers 32:38).

decisions.choice: he lived: Bela as head of his clan
decisions.reason: The singular "he" names Bela, but a man who lived from one town to others far away stands for the clan he headed. Verse 9 goes on with "their livestock".

decisions.choice: Bela's family lived
decisions.reason: Readable says that it was Bela's clan that lived across this area (m2).

records.source: וְלַמִּזְרָ֗ח יָשַׁב֙ עַד־לְב֣וֹאמִדְבָּ֔רָה לְמִן־הַנָּהָ֖ר פְּרָ֑ת כִּ֧י מִקְנֵיהֶ֛ם רָב֖וּ בְּאֶ֥רֶץ גִּלְעָֽד׃
records.gloss: And to the east he dwelt as far as [the] entrance of [the] wilderness, from the river Euphrates, for their livestock had multiplied in [the] land of Gilead.
pieces: To the east he settled as far as the edge of the desert that stretches from the Euphrates River, because their herds had grown large in the land of Gilead.

L.9: And to the east he dwelt as far as the entrance of the wilderness from the river Euphrates, for their livestock had multiplied in the land of Gilead.

R.9: Toward the east they lived as far as the edge of the desert that reaches to the Euphrates River. They spread out because their herds and flocks had grown so large in the land of Gilead.

decisions.choice: the entrance of the wilderness from the Euphrates: the edge of the desert that runs to the Euphrates
decisions.reason: The Reubenites spread east to where the farmland gives way to the great desert that stretches from there to the Euphrates. "From the river" describes the desert's extent; it does not mean they reached the river.

decisions.choice: Gilead: the hill country east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Gilead here is the wider land east of the Jordan where Reuben and Gad settled because it was good for cattle (Numbers 32:1).

decisions.choice: They spread out because
decisions.reason: Readable makes the connection explicit: the growing herds needed more grazing land, so they moved east.

records.source: וּבִימֵ֣י שָׁא֗וּל עָשׂ֤וּ מִלְחָמָה֙ עִם־הַֽהַגְרִאִ֔ים וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ בְּיָדָ֑ם וַיֵּשְׁבוּ֙ בְּאָ֣הֳלֵיהֶ֔ם עַֽל־כָּל־פְּנֵ֖י מִזְרָ֥ח לַגִּלְעָֽד׃פ
records.gloss: And in [the] days of Saul they made war with the Hagrites, and they fell by their hand, and they dwelt in their tents throughout all [the] face of [the] east of Gilead.
pieces: In the days of Saul they made war on the Hagrites, who fell into their power, and they lived in their tents across the whole region east of Gilead.

L.10: And in the days of Saul they made war with the Hagrites, and they fell by their hand, and they dwelt in their tents throughout all the face of the east of Gilead.

R.10: While Saul was king, the Reubenites fought against the Hagrites and defeated them. Then they lived in the Hagrites' tents in all the land east of Gilead.

decisions.choice: the Hagrites: a people of the desert east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: They are named again in verses 19-20 and in Psalm 83:7 among Israel's eastern enemies. The name may link them with Hagar, mother of Ishmael (Genesis 16:15), and verse 19 names them with tribes descended from Ishmael.

decisions.choice: they fell by their hand: they were defeated by them
decisions.reason: To fall by someone's hand is to be overcome by them. "Their hand" is the hand of the Reubenites.

decisions.choice: their tents: the Hagrites' tents
decisions.reason: The Reubenites took over the camps of the people they defeated and lived in them.

decisions.choice: the Reubenites ... the Hagrites' tents
decisions.reason: Readable names who fought and whose tents they were (m3).

records.source: וּבְנֵי־גָ֣ד לְנֶגְדָּ֗ם יָֽשְׁב֛וּ בְּאֶ֥רֶץ הַבָּשָׁ֖ן עַד־סַלְכָֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Gad opposite them dwelt in [the] land of Bashan as far as Salecah.
pieces: The Gadites lived next to them in the land of Bashan as far as Salecah.

L.11: And [the] sons of Gad dwelt opposite them in the land of Bashan as far as Salecah.

R.11: The people of the tribe of Gad lived beside the Reubenites, in the land of Bashan, as far as Salecah.

decisions.choice: Bashan as far as Salecah: the land north of Gilead to its eastern edge
decisions.reason: Bashan is the high plateau north of Gilead; Salecah lay at its eastern border (Deuteronomy 3:10; Joshua 13:11). Joshua 13:24-28 gives Gad land in Gilead; this verse shows Gad also living in part of Bashan.

decisions.choice: opposite them: beside them
decisions.reason: The Gadites' land faced and bordered the land of the Reubenites.

decisions.choice: the Gadites (Balanced); the people of the tribe of Gad (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Sons of Gad" means the members of the tribe.

records.heading: The descendants of Gad

records.source: יוֹאֵ֣ל הָרֹ֔אשׁ וְשָׁפָ֖ם הַמִּשְׁנֶ֑ה וְיַעְנַ֥י וְשָׁפָ֖ט בַּבָּשָֽׁן׃
records.gloss: Joel the head, and Shapham the second, and Janai and Shaphat in Bashan.
pieces: Joel was the chief, Shapham the second, then Janai and Shaphat in Bashan.

L.12: Joel the chief, and Shapham the second, and Janai and Shaphat in Bashan.

R.12: Their leaders in Bashan were Joel, the chief, then Shapham, who was second in rank, and also Janai and Shaphat.

decisions.choice: the second: second in rank
decisions.reason: Joel led the Gadites and Shapham ranked next to him. Janai and Shaphat are named as further leaders.

decisions.choice: Their leaders ... were
decisions.reason: Readable makes the list of names into a sentence.

records.source: וַאֲחֵיהֶ֞ם לְבֵ֣ית אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם מִֽיכָאֵ֡ל וּמְשֻׁלָּ֡ם וְ֠שֶׁבַע וְיוֹרַ֧י וְיַעְכָּ֛ן וְזִ֥יעַ וָעֵ֖בֶר שִׁבְעָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And their brothers by [the] house of their fathers: Michael and Meshullam and Sheba and Jorai and Jacan and Zia and Eber, seven.
pieces: Their relatives by their ancestral families were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia and Eber, seven in all.

L.13: And their brothers by the house of their fathers: Michael and Meshullam and Sheba and Jorai and Jacan and Zia and Eber, seven.

R.13: Their relatives, family by family, were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia and Eber. There were seven of them.

decisions.choice: the house of their fathers: the ancestral family
decisions.reason: A "father's house" is the extended family descended from one forefather, the unit below the clan (Numbers 1:2).

decisions.choice: relatives
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, "brothers" means kinsmen.

records.source: אֵ֣לֶּה׀בְּנֵ֣י אֲבִיחַ֗יִל בֶּן־חוּרִ֡י בֶּן־יָ֠רוֹחַ בֶּן־גִּלְעָ֧ד בֶּן־מִיכָאֵ֛ל בֶּן־יְשִׁישַׁ֥י בֶּן־יַחְדּ֖וֹ בֶּן־בּֽוּז׃
records.gloss: These [were the] sons of Abihail son of Huri, son of Jaroah, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz.
pieces: These were the sons of Abihail son of Huri, son of Jaroah, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz.

L.14: These [were] the sons of Abihail son of Huri, son of Jaroah, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz.

R.14: These men were descended from Abihail. His family line went back through Huri, Jaroah, Gilead, Michael, Jeshishai and Jahdo to Buz.

decisions.choice: these were the sons of Abihail: the seven of verse 13 traced back through their forefathers
decisions.reason: "These" points back to the seven men of verse 13, and "sons" means descendants. The chain then runs back from Abihail through seven generations to Buz.

decisions.choice: Gilead: a man's name here
decisions.reason: Here Gilead is one of the forefathers in the line, not the region named in verses 9, 10 and 16.

decisions.choice: descended from ... His family line went back through
decisions.reason: Readable shows that "sons" means descendants and that each name is the father of the one before it (m1).

records.source: אֲחִי֙ בֶּן־עַבְדִּיאֵ֣ל בֶּן־גּוּנִ֔י רֹ֖אשׁ לְבֵ֥ית אֲבוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: Ahi son of Abdiel, son of Guni, head of [the] house of their fathers.
pieces: Ahi son of Abdiel, son of Guni, was head of their ancestral family.

L.15: Ahi son of Abdiel, son of Guni, [was] head of the house of their fathers.

R.15: Ahi son of Abdiel and grandson of Guni was the head of their family.

decisions.choice: head of the house of their fathers: chief of the ancestral family
decisions.reason: Ahi led the extended family to which the men of verses 13-14 belonged (see verse 13).

decisions.choice: grandson of Guni
decisions.reason: Readable says what the second "son of" means here.

records.source: וַיֵּֽשְׁב֛וּ בַּגִּלְעָ֥ד בַּבָּשָׁ֖ן וּבִבְנֹתֶ֑יהָ וּבְכָֽל־מִגְרְשֵׁ֥י שָׁר֖וֹן עַל־תּוֹצְאוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And they dwelt in Gilead, in Bashan, and in its daughters, and in all [the] pasturelands of Sharon to their ends.
pieces: They lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its villages, and in all the pasturelands of Sharon to their farthest edges.

L.16: And they dwelt in Gilead, in Bashan and in its daughters, and in all the pasturelands of Sharon to their limits.

R.16: They lived in Gilead, in Bashan and the villages around it, and in all the grazing lands of Sharon as far as they reached.

decisions.choice: its daughters: the villages that belonged to a town or region
decisions.reason: Smaller settlements that depended on a town are called its "daughters" (Numbers 21:25; Joshua 15:45).

decisions.choice: Sharon: a grazing region east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: This Sharon lay in Gad's land east of the Jordan; it is not the coastal plain of Sharon (Isaiah 35:2). Its exact place is not known.

decisions.choice: pasturelands: open land for grazing
decisions.reason: The word names the common land around a settlement where flocks were kept (Numbers 35:2-5).

decisions.choice: daughters (Literal); villages (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture; Balanced and Readable give its meaning (m1).

records.source: כֻּלָּם֙ הִתְיַחְשׂ֔וּ בִּימֵ֖י יוֹתָ֣ם מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֑ה וּבִימֵ֖י יָרָבְעָ֥ם מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
records.gloss: All of them were enrolled by genealogy in [the] days of Jotham king of Judah and in [the] days of Jeroboam king of Israel.
pieces: All of them were entered in the genealogies while Jotham was king of Judah and Jeroboam was king of Israel.

L.17: All of them were enrolled in the genealogy in the days of Jotham king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.

R.17: All of them were listed in the family records when Jotham was king of Judah and when Jeroboam was king of Israel.

decisions.choice: Jotham and Jeroboam: kings of the eighth century BC
decisions.reason: Jeroboam is the second king of Israel of that name, son of Jehoash, who reigned forty-one years (2 Kings 14:23). Jotham king of Judah reigned later (2 Kings 15:32-33), though he governed for his father Uzziah before that (2 Kings 15:5). The verse may refer to records made in each of the two reigns.

decisions.choice: enrolled in the genealogy
decisions.reason: As in verse 7: recorded by descent in the tribal register.

records.source: בְּנֵֽי־רְאוּבֵ֨ן וְגָדִ֜י וַחֲצִ֥י שֵֽׁבֶט־מְנַשֶּׁה֮ מִן־בְּנֵי־חַיִל֒ אֲ֠נָשִׁים נֹשְׂאֵ֨י מָגֵ֤ן וְחֶ֨רֶב֙ וְדֹ֣רְכֵי קֶ֔שֶׁת וּלְמוּדֵ֖י מִלְחָמָ֑ה אַרְבָּעִ֨ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֥ה אֶ֛לֶף וּשְׁבַע־מֵא֥וֹת וְשִׁשִּׁ֖ים יֹצְאֵ֥י צָבָֽא׃
records.gloss: [The] sons of Reuben and [the] Gadite[s] and half [the] tribe of Manasseh, of sons of strength, men carrying shield and sword and treading [the] bow and trained [in] war, forty and four thousand and seven hundred and sixty, going out [to the] army.
pieces: The Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh had capable warriors, men who carried shield and sword, drew the bow and were trained for war: 44,760 who could go out to war.

L.18: [The] sons of Reuben and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, of the men of valor, men carrying shield and sword and treading the bow and trained in war, [were] 44,760, going out [to the] army.

R.18: The tribes of Reuben and Gad and half of the tribe of Manasseh had 44,760 skilled soldiers ready to go to war. They carried shields and swords, used bows, and were trained for battle.

decisions.choice: sons of strength: capable fighting men
decisions.reason: "Sons of strength" means men of ability and courage, here able warriors.

decisions.choice: treading the bow: drawing the bow
decisions.reason: A bow was strung or bent by pressing on it with the foot, so "treading the bow" means shooting with it, being an archer.

decisions.choice: 44,760: the total as written
decisions.reason: The total is given as the text has it. On the question of how large such counts in "thousands" were, see Numbers 1:46.

decisions.choice: who could go out to war (Balanced); ready to go to war (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Going out to the army" means fit for military service, worded as in the census lists of Numbers.

records.source: וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ מִלְחָמָ֖ה עִם־הַֽהַגְרִיאִ֑ים וִיט֥וּר וְנָפִ֖ישׁ וְנוֹדָֽב׃
records.gloss: And they made war with the Hagrites and Jetur and Naphish and Nodab.
pieces: They made war on the Hagrites, Jetur, Naphish and Nodab.

L.19: And they made war with the Hagrites and Jetur and Naphish and Nodab.

R.19: They went to war against the Hagrites and the tribes of Jetur, Naphish and Nodab.

decisions.choice: Jetur and Naphish: tribes descended from Ishmael
decisions.reason: Jetur and Naphish are named among the sons of Ishmael (Genesis 25:15; 1 Chronicles 1:31), and the names stand here for the tribes descended from them. Nodab is not named elsewhere.

decisions.choice: the tribes of
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the names are peoples, not single men (m1).

records.source: וַיֵּעָזְר֣וּ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּנָּתְנ֤וּ בְיָדָם֙ הַֽהַגְרִיאִ֔ים וְכֹ֖ל שֶׁ֣עִמָּהֶ֑ם כִּ֠י לֵאלֹהִ֤ים זָעֲקוּ֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְנַעְתּ֥וֹר לָהֶ֖ם כִּי־בָ֥טְחוּ בֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And they were helped against them, and were given into their hand the Hagrites and all who [were] with them, for to God they cried out in the battle, and he was entreated by them, because they trusted in him.
pieces: They received help against them, and the Hagrites and everyone with them were handed over to them, because they called out to God during the battle, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered their prayer, since they trusted in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.20: And they were helped against them, and the Hagrites and all who [were] with them were given into their hand, for they cried out to God in the battle, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was entreated by them, because they trusted in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.20: God helped them against their enemies, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them victory over the Hagrites and all who fought with them. During the battle they had called out to God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered them because they trusted in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: they were helped: helped by God
decisions.reason: The passive does not name the helper, but the rest of the verse and verse 22 show that the help came from God.

decisions.choice: he was entreated by them: he listened to their plea and granted it
decisions.reason: This form of the verb means to let oneself be moved by prayer, to answer a plea (Genesis 25:21; 2 Samuel 24:25).

decisions.choice: because they trusted in him
decisions.reason: Chronicles often shows that crying out to God and relying on him brings victory, and relying on others brings defeat (2 Chronicles 13:18; 14:10; 16:7-8).

decisions.choice: God helped them ... he gave them victory
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who helped and gave the victory (m1), and says "gave them victory over" for "were given into their hand".

records.source: וַיִּשְׁבּ֣וּ מִקְנֵיהֶ֗ם גְּֽמַלֵּיהֶ֞ם חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אֶ֨לֶף֙ וְצֹ֗אן מָאתַ֤יִם וַחֲמִשִּׁים֙ אֶ֔לֶף וַחֲמוֹרִ֖ים אַלְפָּ֑יִם וְנֶ֥פֶשׁ אָדָ֖ם מֵ֥אָה אָֽלֶף׃
records.gloss: And they took captive their livestock: their camels, fifty thousand, and sheep, two hundred and fifty thousand, and donkeys, two thousand, and persons of humankind, a hundred thousand.
pieces: They captured their livestock, 50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep and 2,000 donkeys, and they took 100,000 people captive.

L.21: And they captured their livestock: their camels, 50,000, and sheep, 250,000, and donkeys, 2,000, and human persons, 100,000.

R.21: They took the Hagrites' animals: 50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep and 2,000 donkeys. They took 100,000 people as prisoners too.

decisions.choice: persons of humankind: people
decisions.reason: The phrase sets the human captives apart from the animals just listed.

decisions.choice: the numbers as written
decisions.reason: The figures are given as the text has them (see verse 18).

records.source: כִּֽי־חֲלָלִ֤ים רַבִּים֙ נָפָ֔לוּ כִּ֥י מֵהָאֱלֹהִ֖ים הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וַיֵּשְׁב֥וּ תַחְתֵּיהֶ֖ם עַד־הַגֹּלָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: For slain [ones] many fell, because from God [was] the war; and they dwelt in their place until the exile.
pieces: Many fell dead, because the war was God's doing. And they lived in their place until the exile.

L.22: For many fell slain, because the war [was] from God; and they dwelt in their place until the exile.

R.22: Many of the enemy were killed, because God was fighting the battle. The Reubenites, Gadites and Manassites lived in the Hagrites' land until they were taken into exile.

decisions.choice: the war was from God
decisions.reason: God brought about the war and its outcome. The same conviction is voiced in 1 Samuel 17:47 and 2 Chronicles 20:15: the battle belongs to God.

decisions.choice: until the exile: the exile told in verse 26
decisions.reason: The eastern tribes held the land until the Assyrian king carried them away (verse 26; 2 Kings 15:29).

decisions.choice: The Reubenites, Gadites and Manassites lived in the Hagrites' land
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are and whose place they took.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֗י חֲצִי֙ שֵׁ֣בֶט מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה יָשְׁב֖וּ בָּאָ֑רֶץ מִבָּשָׁ֞ן עַד־בַּ֧עַל חֶרְמ֛וֹן וּשְׂנִ֥יר וְהַר־חֶרְמ֖וֹן הֵ֥מָּה רָבֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of half [the] tribe of Manasseh dwelt in the land; from Bashan to Baal-hermon and Senir and Mount Hermon they were many.
pieces: The members of the half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the land. They grew numerous from Bashan to Baal-hermon, Senir and Mount Hermon.

L.23: And [the] sons of the half-tribe of Manasseh dwelt in the land; from Bashan to Baal-hermon and Senir and Mount Hermon they were many.

R.23: The people of the half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the land. There were many of them, from Bashan to Baal-hermon, Senir and Mount Hermon.

decisions.choice: from Bashan to ... Mount Hermon belongs with "they were many"
decisions.reason: The main division of the verse falls after "in the land". The places that follow tell where the Manassites became numerous.

decisions.choice: Baal-hermon, Senir and Mount Hermon: the Hermon range in the far north
decisions.reason: Senir is the Amorite name for Hermon (Deuteronomy 3:9), and Baal-hermon is named near it (Judges 3:3). The three names probably mark parts of the same mountain range at the northern limit of the land.

records.heading: The half-tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan

records.source: וְאֵ֖לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֣י בֵית־אֲבוֹתָ֑ם וְעֵ֡פֶר וְיִשְׁעִ֡י וֶאֱלִיאֵ֡ל וְ֠עַזְרִיאֵל וְיִרְמְיָ֨ה וְהוֹדַוְיָ֜ה וְיַחְדִּיאֵ֗ל אֲנָשִׁים֙ גִּבּ֣וֹרֵי חַ֔יִל אַנְשֵׁ֣י שֵׁמ֔וֹת רָאשִׁ֖ים לְבֵ֥ית אֲבוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And these [were the] heads of [the] house of their fathers: and Epher and Ishi and Eliel and Azriel and Jeremiah and Hodaviah and Jahdiel, men mighty of strength, men of names, heads of [the] house of their fathers.
pieces: These were the heads of their ancestral families: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah and Jahdiel. All of them were mighty warriors and famous men, heads of their ancestral families.

L.24: And these [were] the heads of the house of their fathers: Epher and Ishi and Eliel and Azriel and Jeremiah and Hodaviah and Jahdiel, men, mighty men of valor, men of names, heads of the house of their fathers.

R.24: These were the leaders of their families: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah and Jahdiel. These men were brave warriors and famous men, and they led their families.

decisions.choice: and Epher: the list begins with "and"
decisions.reason: The first name has "and" before it, which may mean that a name has dropped out before Epher. No surviving Hebrew text supplies one, and the list is translated as it stands.

decisions.choice: men of names: famous men
decisions.reason: To have a name is to be well known (Genesis 6:4; Numbers 16:2).

decisions.choice: Epher, without "and"
decisions.reason: Literal leaves out the "and" before the first name (m1), which cannot be put into an English list.

decisions.choice: mighty men of valor / mighty warriors / brave warriors
decisions.reason: The phrase for proven fighting men has one wording at each level throughout 1 Chronicles (7:2; 8:40; 12:22; 26:6).

records.source: וַיִּֽמְעֲל֔וּ בֵּאלֹהֵ֖י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּזְנ֗וּ אַחֲרֵי֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י עַמֵּי־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־הִשְׁמִ֥יד אֱלֹהִ֖ים מִפְּנֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And they acted unfaithfully against [the] God of their fathers, and they prostituted themselves after [the] gods of [the] peoples of the land, whom destroyed God from before them.
pieces: But they were unfaithful to the God of their {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} and gave themselves like prostitutes to the gods of the peoples of the land, peoples God had destroyed before them.

L.25: But they acted unfaithfully against the God of their fathers, and they prostituted themselves after the gods of the peoples of the land, whom God had destroyed before them.

R.25: But they were unfaithful to the God of their {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}. Like a wife who leaves her husband for other men, they went after the gods of the peoples who had lived in the land, the peoples God had destroyed to make room for them.

decisions.choice: acted unfaithfully (ma'al): broke faith with God
decisions.reason: The word means a breach of trust against God, betraying what is owed to him (Leviticus 5:15; Joshua 7:1). It is a key word in Chronicles for the sin that brings defeat and exile (10:13; 2 Chronicles 36:14).

decisions.choice: prostituted themselves after the gods: broke faith with God for other gods
decisions.reason: As in Judges 2:17, the covenant is pictured as a marriage, and the worship of other gods as a wife's unfaithfulness.

decisions.choice: the peoples of the land: those who lived east of the Jordan before Israel
decisions.reason: These were the Amorite peoples whose land the eastern tribes received (Numbers 21:21-35; 32:33). God had removed them, yet Israel took up their gods.

decisions.choice: gave themselves like prostitutes (Balanced); like a wife who leaves her husband (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Judges 2:17, Balanced keeps the picture as a comparison and Readable explains it as unfaithfulness in marriage (m2).

decisions.choice: to make room for them
decisions.reason: Readable says what "destroyed before them" means: God removed those peoples so that Israel could live in the land.

records.source: וַיָּעַר֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־ר֣וּחַ׀פּ֣וּל מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֗וּר וְאֶת־ר֨וּחַ֙ תִּלְּגַ֤ת פִּלְנֶ֨סֶר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וַיַּגְלֵם֙ לָראוּבֵנִ֣י וְלַגָּדִ֔י וְלַחֲצִ֖י שֵׁ֣בֶט מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה וַ֠יְבִיאֵם לַחְלַ֨ח וְחָב֤וֹר וְהָרָא֙ וּנְהַ֣ר גּוֹזָ֔ן עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And stirred up [the] God of Israel [the] spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and [the] spirit of Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, and he exiled them, the Reubenite[s] and the Gadite[s] and half [the] tribe of Manasseh, and brought them to Halah and Habor and Hara and [the] river of Gozan, until this day.
pieces: So the God of Israel stirred the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, that is, of Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, and he carried them into exile, the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh. He took them to Halah, Habor, Hara and the river of Gozan, and they remain there to this day.

L.26: And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, and he exiled them, the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and brought them to Halah and Habor and Hara and the river of Gozan, to this day.

R.26: So the God of Israel moved Pul king of Assyria, who is also called Tiglath-pileser, to act. He took the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh away as captives. He brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara and the Gozan River, and they are still there to this day.

decisions.choice: Pul ... and Tilgath-pilneser: one king with two names
decisions.reason: The "and" between the names most likely means "that is": the verbs that follow are singular ("he exiled them, and brought them"), and 2 Kings calls the same king Pul (15:19) and Tiglath-pileser (15:29). Pul was the name he used as king of Babylon. The verse could also be read as naming two kings, one after the other.

decisions.choice: God stirred up the spirit: God moved a foreign king to act
decisions.reason: The Assyrian king carried out God's judgment on the tribes' unfaithfulness (verse 25). Chronicles says God stirred up foreign rulers in the same way for judgment and for restoration (2 Chronicles 21:16; 36:22).

decisions.choice: Halah, Habor, Hara and the river of Gozan
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 17:6 and 18:11 name Halah, the Habor, the river of Gozan and the cities of the Medes as the places where the northern tribes were settled. Here the list has Hara, a place not named elsewhere, and the river of Gozan stands as a separate item.

decisions.choice: to this day: the writer's own day
decisions.reason: As in 4:41 and 4:43, "this day" is the time when Chronicles was written, long after the exile.

decisions.choice: Tilgath-pilneser (Literal); that is, Tiglath-pileser / also called Tiglath-pileser (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the "and" and the Chronicles spelling; Balanced and Readable state the reading of m1 and use the spelling of 2 Kings, as in verse 6. Balanced says "stirred the spirit", the same picture of God rousing the king to act.

decisions.choice: they remain there / they are still there
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that "to this day" means the exiles were still in those places.

records.source: בְּנֵ֖י לֵוִ֑י גֵּרְשׁ֕וֹן קְהָ֖ת וּמְרָרִֽי׃
records.gloss: [The] sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.
pieces: The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.

L.27: [The] sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.

R.27: The sons of Levi were Gershon, Kohath and Merari.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: the Hebrew text begins the line of Levi here, as 5:27
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text chapter 5 runs on to verse 41, and the line of the high priests (5:27-41 here) belongs to it. Many Bibles start chapter 6 here and number these verses 6:1-15, and so number the rest of chapter 6 fifteen higher than the Hebrew (Hebrew 6:1 is their 6:16). The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: Gershon, Kohath and Merari: Levi's three sons
decisions.reason: The same three sons head the Levite families in Exodus 6:16 and Numbers 3:17. The list now traces the priests, Levi's descendants through Kohath and Aaron, down to the exile.

records.heading: The line of the high priests

records.source: וּבְנֵ֖י קְהָ֑ת עַמְרָ֣ם יִצְהָ֔ר וְחֶבְר֖וֹן וְעֻזִּיאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Kohath: Amram and Izhar and Hebron and Uzziel.
pieces: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.

L.28: And [the] sons of Kohath: Amram and Izhar and Hebron and Uzziel.

R.28: The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.

decisions.choice: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel
decisions.reason: The same four sons as Exodus 6:18 and Numbers 3:19. The line continues through Amram, Moses' and Aaron's father.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֣י עַמְרָ֔ם אַהֲרֹ֥ן וּמֹשֶׁ֖ה וּמִרְיָ֑םסוּבְנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֔ן נָדָב֙ וַאֲבִיה֔וּא אֶלְעָזָ֖ר וְאִיתָמָֽר׃ס
records.gloss: And [the] children of Amram: Aaron and Moses and Miriam. And [the] sons of Aaron: Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
pieces: The children of Amram: Aaron, Moses and Miriam. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

L.29: And [the] children of Amram: Aaron and Moses and Miriam. And [the] sons of Aaron: Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

R.29: The children of Amram were Aaron, Moses and Miriam. The sons of Aaron were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

decisions.choice: children: sons and a daughter
decisions.reason: The word usually translated "sons" here includes Miriam, Amram's daughter (Numbers 26:59), so it means children.

decisions.choice: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar
decisions.reason: Aaron's four sons, as in Exodus 6:23. Nadab and Abihu died without sons (Leviticus 10:1-2; Numbers 3:4), and the high priesthood passed to Eleazar, whose line follows.

decisions.choice: children
decisions.reason: Every level says "children" because a daughter is included (m1); the word is already inclusive and needs no setting.

records.source: אֶלְעָזָר֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־פִּֽינְחָ֔ס פִּֽינְחָ֖ס הֹלִ֥יד אֶת־אֲבִישֽׁוּעַ׃
records.gloss: Eleazar fathered Phinehas; Phinehas fathered Abishua.
pieces: Eleazar was the father of Phinehas, and Phinehas was the father of Abishua.

L.30: Eleazar begot Phinehas; Phinehas begot Abishua.

R.30: Eleazar was the father of Phinehas. Phinehas was the father of Abishua.

decisions.choice: the line of the high priests from Eleazar
decisions.reason: From here the list follows the chief priests, father to son, from Eleazar to the exile. Like other genealogies it may name the main links and pass over some generations, and it leaves out high priests of other lines, such as Eli, who descended from Ithamar.

decisions.choice: Phinehas: the priest promised a lasting priesthood
decisions.reason: For his zeal at Peor, God gave Phinehas a covenant of lasting priesthood for him and his descendants (Numbers 25:7-13).

decisions.choice: begot (Literal); was the father of (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Chronicles genealogies use one wording for this verb throughout: Literal "begot", Balanced and Readable "was the father of".

records.source: וַאֲבִישׁ֨וּעַ֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־בֻּקִּ֔י וּבֻקִּ֖י הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־עֻזִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And Abishua fathered Bukki; Bukki fathered Uzzi.
pieces: Abishua was the father of Bukki, and Bukki was the father of Uzzi.

L.31: And Abishua begot Bukki; Bukki begot Uzzi.

R.31: Abishua was the father of Bukki. Bukki was the father of Uzzi.

decisions.choice: Bukki and Uzzi: known only from the priestly lists
decisions.reason: Abishua, Bukki and Uzzi appear again in 6:35-36 and in Ezra's line of descent (Ezra 7:4-5).

records.source: וְעֻזִּי֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־זְרַֽחְיָ֔ה וּֽזְרַֽחְיָ֖ה הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־מְרָיֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And Uzzi fathered Zerahiah; Zerahiah fathered Meraioth.
pieces: Uzzi was the father of Zerahiah, and Zerahiah was the father of Meraioth.

L.32: And Uzzi begot Zerahiah; Zerahiah begot Meraioth.

R.32: Uzzi was the father of Zerahiah. Zerahiah was the father of Meraioth.

decisions.choice: Zerahiah and Meraioth
decisions.reason: These names also appear in Ezra's line of descent (Ezra 7:3-4).

pieces: Meraioth was the father of Amariah, and Amariah was the father of Ahitub.

L.33: Meraioth begot Amariah; Amariah begot Ahitub.

R.33: Meraioth was the father of Amariah. Amariah was the father of Ahitub.

decisions.choice: Amariah and Ahitub: names not in Ezra's line here
decisions.reason: Ezra 7:3 passes from Meraioth straight to a later Azariah, leaving out the names of verses 33-35. Shortened lines of descent like this are common in genealogies.

pieces: Ahitub was the father of Zadok, and Zadok was the father of Ahimaaz.

L.34: And Ahitub begot Zadok; Zadok begot Ahimaaz.

R.34: Ahitub was the father of Zadok. Zadok was the father of Ahimaaz.

decisions.choice: Zadok and Ahimaaz: priests in the days of David
decisions.reason: Zadok son of Ahitub was priest under David (2 Samuel 8:17) and became chief priest under Solomon (1 Kings 2:35). His son Ahimaaz carried news to David during Absalom's revolt (2 Samuel 15:27; 18:19).

records.source: וַאֲחִימַ֨עַץ֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־עֲזַרְיָ֔ה וַעֲזַרְיָ֖ה הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־יוֹחָנָֽן׃
records.gloss: And Ahimaaz fathered Azariah; Azariah fathered Johanan.
pieces: Ahimaaz was the father of Azariah, and Azariah was the father of Johanan.

L.35: And Ahimaaz begot Azariah; Azariah begot Johanan.

R.35: Ahimaaz was the father of Azariah. Azariah was the father of Johanan.

decisions.choice: Azariah and Johanan
decisions.reason: An Azariah son of Zadok is named as priest among Solomon's officials (1 Kings 4:2); "son" may mean grandson there, making him this Azariah son of Ahimaaz.

records.source: וְיוֹחָנָ֖ן הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־עֲזַרְיָ֑ה ה֚וּא אֲשֶׁ֣ר כִּהֵ֔ן בַּבַּ֕יִת אֲשֶׁר־בָּנָ֥ה שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: And Johanan fathered Azariah; he [is the one] who served as priest in the house that built Solomon in Jerusalem.
pieces: Johanan was the father of Azariah. It was he who was priest in the temple Solomon built in Jerusalem.

L.36: And Johanan begot Azariah; he [is the one] who served as priest in the house that Solomon built in Jerusalem.

R.36: Johanan was the father of Azariah. Azariah served as priest in the temple Solomon built in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: he who served as priest: said of Azariah son of Johanan
alternatives: the note first belonged to Azariah son of Ahimaaz (verse 35)
decisions.reason: As the text stands, the note belongs to Azariah son of Johanan. But the Azariah who served in Solomon's time was the grandson of Zadok (verses 34-35; 1 Kings 4:2), so the note may first have stood after verse 35 and been moved in copying. Or it may mean that this later Azariah was a notable priest of the temple.

decisions.choice: the house: the temple
decisions.reason: "The house that Solomon built" is the temple of the LORD in Jerusalem (1 Kings 6:1).

decisions.choice: temple
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "temple" for "house" (m2).

pieces: Azariah was the father of Amariah, and Amariah was the father of Ahitub.

L.37: And Azariah begot Amariah; Amariah begot Ahitub.

R.37: Azariah was the father of Amariah. Amariah was the father of Ahitub.

decisions.choice: Azariah, Amariah, Ahitub: names that recur in the family
decisions.reason: The priestly family reused names, so a second Amariah and Ahitub follow the first ones of verse 33. An Amariah was chief priest under Jehoshaphat (2 Chronicles 19:11).

records.gloss: And Ahitub fathered Zadok; Zadok fathered Shallum.
pieces: Ahitub was the father of Zadok, and Zadok was the father of Shallum.

L.38: And Ahitub begot Zadok; Zadok begot Shallum.

R.38: Ahitub was the father of Zadok. Zadok was the father of Shallum.

decisions.choice: a second Zadok; Shallum
decisions.reason: This Zadok is a later descendant of the Zadok of verse 34. Shallum is called Meshullam in 9:11 and Nehemiah 11:11.

pieces: Shallum was the father of Hilkiah, and Hilkiah was the father of Azariah.

L.39: And Shallum begot Hilkiah; Hilkiah begot Azariah.

R.39: Shallum was the father of Hilkiah. Hilkiah was the father of Azariah.

decisions.choice: Hilkiah: the high priest in the days of Josiah
decisions.reason: Hilkiah found the book of the law in the temple during Josiah's reign (2 Kings 22:4, 8).

records.source: וַעֲזַרְיָה֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־שְׂרָיָ֔ה וּשְׂרָיָ֖ה הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־יְהוֹצָדָֽק׃

pieces: Azariah was the father of Seraiah, and Seraiah was the father of Jehozadak.

L.40: And Azariah begot Seraiah; Seraiah begot Jehozadak.

R.40: Azariah was the father of Seraiah. Seraiah was the father of Jehozadak.

decisions.choice: Seraiah and Jehozadak: the last high priests before the exile
decisions.reason: Seraiah was chief priest when Jerusalem fell, and the Babylonians put him to death at Riblah (2 Kings 25:18-21). His son Jehozadak was the father of Joshua, the high priest after the return (Haggai 1:1).

records.source: וִיהוֹצָדָ֣ק הָלַ֔ךְ בְּהַגְל֣וֹת יְהוָ֔ה אֶת־יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם בְּיַ֖ד נְבֻכַדְנֶאצַּֽר׃ס
records.gloss: And Jehozadak went when exiled Yahweh Judah and Jerusalem by [the] hand of Nebuchadnezzar.
pieces: Jehozadak went into exile when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} exiled Judah and Jerusalem through Nebuchadnezzar.

L.41: And Jehozadak went when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} exiled Judah and Jerusalem by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.

R.41: Jehozadak was taken away when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} used Nebuchadnezzar to send the people of Judah and Jerusalem into exile.

decisions.choice: went: went into exile
decisions.reason: The verb "went" stands alone, and the rest of the verse shows where: Jehozadak was among those carried off to Babylon.

decisions.choice: the LORD exiled Judah by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar
decisions.reason: The LORD is the one who sends his people into exile, and the king of Babylon is the means he uses, as the eastern tribes went into exile through the king of Assyria (verse 26; 2 Kings 24:20; 2 Chronicles 36:17).

decisions.choice: went into exile (Balanced); was taken away (Readable); through / used Nebuchadnezzar
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where Jehozadak went (m1). For "by the hand of", Balanced says "through" and Readable "used", since the hand stands for the agent God used (m2).
